title: Annual shallow earthquake counts showed no clear excess alignment across spatial cells in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested annual global earthquake count variance against independent local annual histories. We used 10,473 USGS ComCat events with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth 0-70 km in 2000-2025. For a 20-degree spatial grid, global annual variance was 0.958 times the sum of local variances. Independent circular shifts of cell histories gave an upper-tail p value of 0.521. Twelve grid tests and their linear-trend checks gave no clear excess. Counts had variance 11.39 times their mean, so Poisson overdispersion did not imply excess annual alignment across cells. A magnitude-6 check also gave no clear excess. This result is conditional on independent rotation phases. It does not prove independence or exclude remote triggering. Short records, catalog changes, cyclic timing assumptions and grid boundaries limit inference. Code, provenance, all whole-sample simulation draws, an audit and a figure are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Annual counts, the primary rotation distribution, and grid sensitivity. Ratios compare global variance with the sum of cell variances. Null ranges are conditional, not physical confidence limits.

citations.reason: Published grid sensitivity motivated boundary checks. Source records overlap; this is not independent replication.
